*I spent a total of around 20-30 hours on this lab. Most of this time was spent on the test benches, refactoring my code, and doing this forsaken lab report*

## Introduction
In this lab, the [circuit from lab 2](lab2.qmd) consisting of a multiplexed two digit seven segment
display and a keypad, was slightly modified and was given some new functionality. This functionality
came in the form of programming the [UPduino
v3.1](https://github.com/tinyvision-ai-inc/upduino-v3.0) to read in key presses from the 4x4 keypad
and record the corresponding hexadecimal numbers onto the seven segment display. This involved
multiple different kinds of finite state machines, synchronizers, a debounce mechanism, and lots of
testing. This was my first opportunity to tackle a more complex (has many intertwined parts) problem
using an FPGA. Overall, it went well (though the testbench took very long).

## Design and Testing Methodology

### Main FSM

This FSM has the following state transition diagram (assume outputs are 0 unless mentioned otherwise):

![The main FSM's state transition diagram describes how this system reacts to keypresses](../media/lab3/state_transition_diagram.jpg){#fig-block-top}

In table from, this would be:

+------------------------+-----------------------+------------------------+-------------------------+
| Current state          | Event/inputs          | Next state             | Output(s)               |
+========================+=======================+========================+=========================+
| `onekeypressed_disp`   | ALWAYS                | `onekeypressed_nodisp` | `display_next_char = 1` |
+------------------------+-----------------------+------------------------+-------------------------+
| `onekeypressed_nodisp` | IF `~one_key_pressed` | `read_keypad`          | none                    |
+------------------------+-----------------------+------------------------+-------------------------+
| `onekeypressed_nodisp` | ELSE (see above)      | `onekeypressed_nodisp` | none                    |
+------------------------+-----------------------+------------------------+-------------------------+
| `read_keypad`          | IF `one_key_pressed`  | `onekeypressed_disp`   | none                    |
+------------------------+-----------------------+------------------------+-------------------------+
| `read_keypad`          | ELSE (see above)      | `read_keypad`          | none                    |
+------------------------+-----------------------+------------------------+-------------------------+

In the case of this table, `one_key_pressed` is a variable that is HIGH when only one slot in the
stable (already synchronized and debounced) array of key statuses is HIGH (pressed). Else, it is
low. The systemverilog snippet for that is:
```systemverilog
logic one_key_pressed; // 1 clock cycle delay for this logic to avoid FPGA timing constraint violations & increase legibility
    always_ff @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) one_key_pressed <= 'b0;
        else one_key_pressed <= ((key_status != 0) && ((key_status & (key_status - 1)) == 0));
    end
```

Though the code in this lab also *technically* contains other finite state machines, only this one
is drawn as doing so for the others would obscure their meaning. The debouncer is technically an
FSM, but it is also a simple shift-register, which is a more useful model. A similar thing applies
to all of the counters, or the buffers, or the synchronizer. Thinking of those parts in terms of
their function is more useful than thinking of those parts in terms of their behaviour given a
certain input.

### HDL Design
The overarching design was structured in five modules (for more information see @sec-block). Every
module is commented in such a way that its function is clear.

### HDL Testing
The HDL code was tested module-by-module. As a lot of the modules were refactored (and some even
modified), most test-benches from previous labs needed to be updated. Some special features this
time around include the use of `$past` statements instead of `force` and `release` whenever possible
in order to assert if enable is properly functioning. Additionally, the tests at the top module were
more sparse, in favor of comprehensive per-module testing. Every reasonable function that I could
think of was tested. I was up all night writing and modifying these test benches.

### Hardware Design
The Hardware Design was almost identical to [that of lab 2](lab2.qmd), therefore the minutia will
not be repeated here. The additional DIP switches were removed (or disabled), as were the LED's.
The breadboard side of things was the same, except for the diodes being moved from the columns of
the keypad matrix to the rows of the keyboard matrix (as rows and columns were flipped in lab 2).

For more details see the schematic in @sec-schematic.

## Conclusion
I managed to successfully implement all of the functionality required by the [lab
instructions](https://hmc-e155.github.io/lab/lab3/). I will note that the specifications were a bit
unclear as to what the exact expected behaviour is under different multi-press/release situations.
Therefore my design technically allows a key to be registered more than once despite only being
pressed once. I would consider this to be a minor detail that is easily fixable by adding one
additional state to the `main_fsm`.

As mentioned at the top, I spent a total of around 20-30 hours on this lab. I was lucky on the whole
logic/coding section but spent a very long time refactoring my code to be more legible, testing all
of the new sub-modules, making the artifacts for this report, and helping others debug their (very
different) approaches to the problem presented within this lab.

### AI Prototype Summary
I chose to prompt Google Gemini with the HMC education account. The initial prompt was was:

> Target device: Lattice iCE40 UP5K FPGA with internal high-speed oscillator (~20 MHz).
> 
> Write synthesizable SystemVerilog to scan a 4x4 matrix keypad and display the last two hex keys
> pressed on a dual 7‑segment display. Implement:
> 
> A clock divider that derives a scan clock on the order of 100–200 Hz from the internal oscillator.
> A keypad scanning controller that iterates one active‑low column at a time and samples active‑low
> rows, registering at most one key per press (debounce‑by‑design), ignoring additional presses
> while any key is held, and allowing a new registration only after release. A top level that
> updates two hex digits (older and most recent) when a new key is registered and drives a
> time‑multiplexed two‑digit 7‑segment display without visible flicker and with balanced brightness.
> Use idiomatic SystemVerilog (e.g., logic, always_ff, enumerated states for FSMs). Provide clean
> module boundaries and keep all state synchronous. Include brief comments explaining the design
> choices.
>
> Write SystemVerilog HDL to time multiplex a single seven segment decoder (that decodes from four
> bits to a common anode seven segment display) to decode two sets of input bits and drive two sets
> of seven output bits.


::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Initial AI Response: Google Gemini Free (no thinking)

Here is a complete, self-contained, synthesizable SystemVerilog implementation tailored for the
Lattice iCE40 UltraPlus (UP5K).

The design uses the Lattice `HSOSC` primitive, a synchronous FSM-based matrix scanner, and a
time-multiplexed 7-segment display driver.

### System Architecture
```
+---------------------------------------------------------+
                       | Keypad Controller Top                                   |
                       |                                                         |
  +---------------+    |  +---------------+    +---------------+    +---------+  |    +-------------------+
  | Lattice HSOSC |    |  | Clock         |    | Keypad        |    | Display |  |    | Dual 7-Seg Display|
  |  Primitive    |--->|->| Divider       |--->| Scanner FSM   |--->| Driver  |--|--->| (Anodes & Cathodes|
  +---------------+    |  | (~200 Hz)     |    | (Active-Low)  |    | (Multiplex)|  |    +-------------------+
                       |  +---------------+    +---------------+    +---------+  |
                       +---------------------------------------------------------+
                                 ^                    ^
                                 |                    |
                           keypad_row           keypad_col
```

### Keypad Scanner Module

```systemverilog
// Keypad Matrix Scanner FSM
// Debounce-by-design: By running the FSM on a 200 Hz scan clock (5 ms per column / 20 ms per full matrix loop),
// mechanical contact bounce (<10 ms) resolves naturally without needing dedicated debounce counters.
module keypad_scanner (
    input  logic       clk_scan,     // ~100-200 Hz clock derived from oscillator
    input  logic       rst_n,        // Asynchronous reset (active-low)
    input  logic [3:0] keypad_row,   // Matrix rows (active-low with pull-ups)
    output logic [3:0] keypad_col,   // Matrix columns (active-low output)
    output logic [3:0] key_code,     // Detected key Hex value (0x0 - 0xF)
    output logic       key_valid     // 1-cycle pulse when a new key press is registered
);

    // Key map matrix lookup table:
    // Keypad layout:
    // [ '1'(0x1), '2'(0x2), '3'(0x3), 'A'(0xA) ]
    // [ '4'(0x4), '5'(0x5), '6'(0x6), 'B'(0xB) ]
    // [ '7'(0x7), '8'(0x8), '9'(0x9), 'C'(0xC) ]
    // [ 'E'(0xE), '0'(0x0), 'F'(0xF), 'D'(0xD) ]  (E=* and F=# mapped to hex)

    // FSM State Definition
    typedef enum logic [1:0] {
        SCAN      = 2'b00,
        KEY_FOUND = 2'b01,
        WAIT_RELEASE = 2'b10
    } state_e;

    state_e state;
    logic [1:0] col_idx;
    logic [3:0] registered_key;

    // Drive active-low column scan signal
    always_comb begin
        keypad_col = 4'b1111;
        keypad_col[col_idx] = 1'b0;
    end

    // FSM State and Scan Control Logic
    always_ff @(posedge clk_scan or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            state          <= SCAN;
            col_idx        <= 2'd0;
            registered_key <= 4'h0;
            key_code       <= 4'h0;
            key_valid      <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            key_valid <= 1'b0; // Default pulse auto-clear

            case (state)
                SCAN: begin
                    // Check if any row is low (key pressed in current column)
                    if (keypad_row != 4'b1111) begin
                        state <= KEY_FOUND;
                    end else begin
                        col_idx <= col_idx + 1'b1; // Advance to next column
                    end
                end

                KEY_FOUND: begin
                    // Map active row/col to 4-bit hex value
                    case ({col_idx, keypad_row})
                        // Column 0
                        6'b00_1110: registered_key <= 4'h1;
                        6'b00_1101: registered_key <= 4'h4;
                        6'b00_1011: registered_key <= 4'h7;
                        6'b00_0111: registered_key <= 4'hE; // '*' key
                        // Column 1
                        6'b01_1110: registered_key <= 4'h2;
                        6'b01_1101: registered_key <= 4'h5;
                        6'b01_1011: registered_key <= 4'h8;
                        6'b01_0111: registered_key <= 4'h0;
                        // Column 2
                        6'b10_1110: registered_key <= 4'h3;
                        6'b10_1101: registered_key <= 4'h6;
                        6'b10_1011: registered_key <= 4'h9;
                        6'b10_0111: registered_key <= 4'hF; // '#' key
                        // Column 3
                        6'b11_1110: registered_key <= 4'hA;
                        6'b11_1101: registered_key <= 4'hB;
                        6'b11_1011: registered_key <= 4'hC;
                        6'b11_0111: registered_key <= 4'hD;
                        default:    registered_key <= 4'h0;
                    endcase

                    key_code  <= registered_key;
                    key_valid <= 1'b1; // Emit single registration pulse
                    state     <= WAIT_RELEASE;
                end

                WAIT_RELEASE: begin
                    // Wait until ALL keys in ALL columns are fully released
                    // Pull all columns LOW simultaneously to test for any row closure
                    keypad_col <= 4'b0000;
                    if (keypad_row == 4'b1111) begin
                        state   <= SCAN;
                        col_idx <= 2'd0;
                    end
                end

                default: state <= SCAN;
            endcase
        end
    end

endmodule
```

### Dual 7-Segment Display Controller

```systemverilog
// Multiplexed Dual 7-Segment Display Controller
module display_driver (
    input  logic       clk_fast,    // Fast System Clock (~20 MHz)
    input  logic       rst_n,       // Active-low reset
    input  logic [3:0] digit_high,  // Older Hex digit
    input  logic [3:0] digit_low,   // Most recent Hex digit
    output logic [1:0] digit_anode, // Active-low digit selects [1]=Digit 1, [0]=Digit 0
    output logic [6:0] seg_cathodes // Active-low cathodes [A, B, C, D, E, F, G]
);

    // Refresh rate control:
    // ~20 MHz / 2^16 = ~305 Hz refresh rate per digit (~152 Hz per frame), well above flicker threshold (>60 Hz).
    logic [16:0] refresh_counter;
    logic        active_digit;
    logic [3:0]  hex_to_decode;
    logic [6:0]  decoded_segments;

    always_ff @(posedge clk_fast or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n)
            refresh_counter <= '0;
        else
            refresh_counter <= refresh_counter + 1'b1;
    end

    assign active_digit = refresh_counter[16];

    // Select active hex nibble
    assign hex_to_decode = active_digit ? digit_high : digit_low;

    // Hex to 7-Segment Decoder (active-low segments: A, B, C, D, E, F, G)
    always_comb begin
        case (hex_to_decode)
            4'h0: decoded_segments = 7'b000_0001; // 0
            4'h1: decoded_segments = 7'b100_1111; // 1
            4'h2: decoded_segments = 7'b001_0010; // 2
            4'h3: decoded_segments = 7'b000_0110; // 3
            4'h4: decoded_segments = 7'b100_1100; // 4
            4'h5: decoded_segments = 7'b010_0100; // 5
            4'h6: decoded_segments = 7'b010_0000; // 6
            4'h7: decoded_segments = 7'b000_1101; // 7
            4'h8: decoded_segments = 7'b000_0000; // 8
            4'h9: decoded_segments = 7'b000_0100; // 9
            4'hA: decoded_segments = 7'b000_1000; // A
            4'hB: decoded_segments = 7'b110_0000; // b
            4'hC: decoded_segments = 7'b011_0001; // C
            4'hD: decoded_segments = 7'b100_0010; // d
            4'hE: decoded_segments = 7'b011_0000; // E
            4'hF: decoded_segments = 7'b011_1000; // F
            default: decoded_segments = 7'b111_1111;
        endcase
    end

    // Ghosting prevention / Equalized Brightness via brief blanking during multiplex transitions
    logic blanking;
    assign blanking = (refresh_counter[15:0] < 16'd500); // ~25 us guard-band window

    always_comb begin
        if (blanking) begin
            digit_anode  = 2'b11;        // Disable both anodes
            seg_cathodes = 7'b111_1111;  // Disable segments
        end else begin
            digit_anode  = active_digit ? 2'b10 : 2'b01;
            seg_cathodes = decoded_segments;
        end
    end

endmodule
```

### Top-Level Integration
This module instantiates the `HSOSC` primitive, drives clock division, shifts new keypresses into
the 2-digit history register, and ties together the scanner and display modules.

```systemverilog
// Top-Level Keypad and Display System
module top_keypad_display (
    input  logic       rst_n,        // Active-low asynchronous reset pin
    input  logic [3:0] keypad_row,   // Input matrix rows (external weak pull-ups enabled)
    output logic [3:0] keypad_col,   // Output matrix columns
    output logic [1:0] digit_anode,  // Digit select anodes
    output logic [6:0] seg_cathodes  // Segment cathodes
);

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 1. Lattice iCE40 UltraPlus Internal High-Speed Oscillator (HSOSC)
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    logic sys_clk;

    // HSOSC Primitive Configuration:
    // CLKHF_DIV = "0b00" -> 48 MHz
    // CLKHF_DIV = "0b01" -> 24 MHz
    // CLKHF_DIV = "0b10" -> 12 MHz
    // CLKHF_DIV = "0b11" -> 6 MHz
    HSOSC #(
        .CLKHF_DIV("0b01") // Configured for ~24 MHz / nominally ~20 MHz nominal operation
    ) u_hsosc (
        .CLKHFPU(1'b1),    // Power-up oscillator
        .CLKHFEN(1'b1),    // Enable output
        .CLKHF(sys_clk)    // Output clock signal
    );

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 2. Synchronous Clock Divider (~200 Hz scan clock)
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 24 MHz / (2 * 60,000) = 200 Hz
    localparam int CLK_DIV_LIMIT = 60000 - 1;

    logic [15:0] clk_cnt;
    logic        clk_scan;

    always_ff @(posedge sys_clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            clk_cnt  <= '0;
            clk_scan <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            if (clk_cnt == CLK_DIV_LIMIT) begin
                clk_cnt  <= '0;
                clk_scan <= ~clk_scan; // Toggle scan clock
            end else begin
                clk_cnt  <= clk_cnt + 1'b1;
            end
        end
    end

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 3. Matrix Keypad Scanner Instantiation
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    logic [3:0] current_key;
    logic       key_valid;

    keypad_scanner u_keypad_scanner (
        .clk_scan   (clk_scan),
        .rst_n      (rst_n),
        .keypad_row (keypad_row),
        .keypad_col (keypad_col),
        .key_code   (current_key),
        .key_valid  (key_valid)
    );

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 4. Shift Register for Key History
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    logic [3:0] digit_high; // Older key
    logic [3:0] digit_low;  // Most recent key

    always_ff @(posedge sys_clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            digit_high <= 4'h0;
            digit_low  <= 4'h0;
        end else if (key_valid) begin
            digit_high <= digit_low;    // Shift low digit to high digit
            digit_low  <= current_key;  // Push new key into low digit
        end
    end

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 5. Multiplexed Display Driver Instantiation
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    display_driver u_display_driver (
        .clk_fast     (sys_clk),
        .rst_n        (rst_n),
        .digit_high   (digit_high),
        .digit_low    (digit_low),
        .digit_anode  (digit_anode),
        .seg_cathodes (seg_cathodes)
    );

endmodule
```

### Implementation Details & Design Choices
1. Lattice iCE40 UP5K Oscillator (HSOSC):
    - Uses the hard IP block to generate a system clock without requiring external crystal hardware. It
      is set to 24 MHz nominal frequency via parameter CLKHF_DIV = "0b01".
2. Debounce-by-Design FSM:
    - Instead of using large counters, debouncing is inherent to the scan rate. Scanning columns at 200 Hz
    means an entire 4x4 sweep takes 20 ms. Switch contact bounces (<10 ms) decay completely between
    consecutive samples.
3. Single Key & Roll-over Protection:
    - When a valid key is sampled, the FSM enters `WAIT_RELEASE` and pulls all columns active-low
      (`4'b0000`). It locks out additional key detections until all row inputs return high (`4'b1111`),
      preventing double-registration when keys are held down.
4. Anti-Ghosting Guard Band:
    - A short dead-time (blanking) is asserted during digit switches in display_driver. This gives
      the FPGA output buffers and driver transistors time to fully discharge parasitic capacitive
      charges before turning on the next digit, eliminating ghosting artifacts.
:::

This first stab that the LLM took was a bit of a mess to be honest. A thing that I personally was
very intentional about was keeping every sub-module active HIGH in order to be consistent and not
end up confusing things as I connect multiple blocks together. This kind of discipline is not really
present in this AI answer. Additionally, the keypad FSM is way too bulky. That all being said, the
general logic that the LLM came up with for the FSM is the same thing that I initially thought of.

Interestingly enough, this is the second time that the LLM outputs async code. Granted, it does this
by diving down the clock and feeding that as a module input. BUT this is a dangerous habit to get
into, especially because there (usually) won't be must of a problem when you do this.

> Target device: Lattice iCE40 UP5K FPGA.
> 
> Overall Goal: Write SystemVerilog to scan a 4x4 matrix keypad and display the last two hex keys
> pressed on a dual 7 segment display.
> 
> Current Goal: Write a synthesizable SystemVerilog module that produces a one‑shot registration
> signal for the keypad system. Behavior:
> 
> When a key press is first detected, capture the current key code and assert a single‑cycle “new
> key” pulse. While any key remains pressed, do not accept additional keys. Only after keys are
> released should a subsequent press be recognized. This should handle debouncing of the keys.
> Implement as a small synchronous FSM with enumerated states and glitch‑free outputs. Keep names
> and interfaces reasonable; do not assume any hidden modules beyond what you define here.

> Target device: Lattice iCE40 UP5K FPGA.
> 
> Write a synthesizable SystemVerilog module that cycles through keypad columns (active‑low, one at
> a time) and samples rows (active‑low) to detect a single key at a time. Behavior:
> 
> Iterate columns at a suitable scan rate derived from the divided clock and sample rows. When a key
> is detected, report a stable key code consistent with a standard 4x4 keypad layout and maintain it
> while the key remains pressed. Provide a boolean signal indicating whether any key is currently
> pressed. Use clean state encoding and synchronous logic; avoid combinational feedback and latches.

> Target device: Lattice iCE40 UP5K FPGA with internal oscillator as the root clock source.
> 
> Write a top‑level SystemVerilog module that instantiates the scanner and one‑shot modules, shifts
> the last two keys (older ← most recent; most recent ← new), and drives a multiplexed two‑digit
> seven‑segment display. Requirements:
> 
> Update the displayed digits only when a new key is registered. Ensure equal apparent brightness
> and no visible flicker. Keep all logic synthesizable and synchronous; use idiomatic SystemVerilog
> constructs. Provide any small clock‑enable or divider logic you need. You can also assume that a
> sevenSegment module exists that takes a 4 bit input and outputs the 7 segments.

Here is the complete SystemVerilog module for key debouncing, edge detection, and release
validation. It uses a synchronous state machine paired with a counter-based debouncer to ensure
single-cycle, glitch-free key registration.

```systemverilog
module keypad_oneshot #(
    parameter int CLK_FREQ_HZ = 12_000_000, // 12 MHz default for iCE40
    parameter int DEBOUNCE_MS = 10          // 10 ms debounce time
)(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    input  logic       raw_key_valid, // 1 when any key is currently detected pressed
    input  logic [3:0] raw_key_code,  // Active key code from scanner
    output logic       new_key_strobe, // 1-cycle pulse when a new key is accepted
    output logic [3:0] key_code        // Registered key code associated with strobe
);

    // Calculate count threshold for debouncing
    localparam int DEBOUNCE_CYCLES = (CLK_FREQ_HZ / 1000) * DEBOUNCE_MS;
    localparam int COUNTER_WIDTH  = $clog2(DEBOUNCE_CYCLES);

    // FSM State Encoding
    typedef enum logic [1:0] {
        IDLE        = 2'b00, // Waiting for a stable key press
        STROBE      = 2'b01, // Generating single-cycle output pulse
        WAIT_RELEASE= 2'b10  // Lock out until keys are fully released
    } state_e;

    state_e state_reg, state_next;

    // Debounce Counter & Stable Logic
    logic [COUNTER_WIDTH-1:0] timer_reg;
    logic timer_max;
    logic raw_key_valid_sync1, raw_key_valid_sync;

    // Double-flop synchronizer to prevent metastability on async keypad inputs
    always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            raw_key_valid_sync1 <= 1'b0;
            raw_key_valid_sync  <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            raw_key_valid_sync1 <= raw_key_valid;
            raw_key_valid_sync  <= raw_key_valid_sync1;
        end
    end

    // Debounce Timer Logic
    always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            timer_reg <= '0;
        end else begin
            // Reset timer whenever the key state transitions, otherwise count up to MAX
            if ((state_reg == IDLE && !raw_key_valid_sync) || 
                (state_reg == WAIT_RELEASE && raw_key_valid_sync)) begin
                timer_reg <= '0;
            end else if (!timer_max) begin
                timer_reg <= timer_reg + 1'b1;
            end
        end
    end

    assign timer_max = (timer_reg >= DEBOUNCE_CYCLES - 1);

    // FSM State Register & Output Registering (Glitch-Free)
    always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            state_reg      <= IDLE;
            new_key_strobe <= 1'b0;
            key_code       <= 4'h0;
        end else begin
            state_reg <= state_next;

            // Registered outputs derived strictly from state transitions
            if (state_reg == IDLE && state_next == STROBE) begin
                new_key_strobe <= 1'b1;
                key_code       <= raw_key_code; // Sample key code on valid press
            end else begin
                new_key_strobe <= 1 me0; // Auto-clear after 1 cycle
            end
        end
    end

    // FSM Next-State Combinational Logic
    always_comb begin
        state_next = state_reg;

        case (state_reg)
            IDLE: begin
                // Require key press to remain stable for DEBOUNCE_MS before moving on
                if (raw_key_valid_sync && timer_max) begin
                    state_next = STROBE;
                end
            end

            STROBE: begin
                // Transition immediately after 1 cycle
                state_next = WAIT_RELEASE;
            end

            WAIT_RELEASE: begin
                // Require key release to remain stable for DEBOUNCE_MS before returning to IDLE
                if (!raw_key_valid_sync && timer_max) begin
                    state_next = IDLE;
                end
            end

            default: state_next = IDLE;
        endcase
    end

endmodule
```

### Key Architectural Details
- **Metastability Guard:** Keypad inputs originate from mechanical switches. A 2-stage synchronizer
  (`raw_key_valid_sync`) guards the internal state logic against asynchronous setup/hold violations.
- **Symmetrical Debouncing:** The `timer_reg` counter validates both initial key closures (press
  debounce) and mechanical bounces upon opening (release debounce).
- **Glitch-Free Registered Outputs:** Both `new_key_strobe` and `key_code` are assigned inside a
  sequential (`always_ff`) block. `new_key_strobe` asserts for exactly one clock cycle as the FSM
  moves from `IDLE` to `STROBE`.
- **Single-Key Lockout:** The state machine transitions to `WAIT_RELEASE` immediately following the
  strobe cycle and holds there until the keypad returns to an unpressed state (`raw_key_valid = 0`)
  for the full debounce duration.

Here is the complete SystemVerilog matrix scanner module designed for the Lattice iCE40 UP5K. It
continuously drives active-low columns, samples active-low rows, decodes key presses into standard
4x4 hex values, and pauses scanning while a key is held to maintain a stable output.

```systemverilog
module keypad_scanner #(
    parameter int CLK_FREQ_HZ = 12_000_000, // 12 MHz default iCE40 clock
    parameter int SCAN_FREQ_HZ = 1000       // 1 kHz scan rate per column
)(
    input  logic       clk,
    input  logic       rst_n,
    // Matrix physical pins (Active-Low)
    input  logic [3:0] row_pins,            // Internal pull-ups enabled in PCF
    output logic [3:0] col_pins,            // Driven active-low one at a time
    // Decoded Outputs
    output logic       raw_key_valid,       // High while any key is detected pressed
    output logic [3:0] raw_key_code         // Active key code (0-F)
);

    // Clock divider for scanning period
    localparam int CLK_DIV_CYCLES = CLK_FREQ_HZ / SCAN_FREQ_HZ;
    localparam int CLK_DIV_WIDTH  = $clog2(CLK_DIV_CYCLES);

    logic [CLK_DIV_WIDTH-1:0] scan_timer;
    logic scan_tick;

    // Synchronizers for asynchronous row inputs
    logic [3:0] row_sync1, row_sync2;

    // Scan state registers
    logic [1:0] col_select;
    logic [3:0] col_pins_reg;
    logic       key_valid_reg;
    logic [3:0] key_code_reg;

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 1. Clock Divider for Column Scanning
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            scan_timer <= '0;
            scan_tick  <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            if (scan_timer >= CLK_DIV_CYCLES - 1) begin
                scan_timer <= '0;
                scan_tick  <= 1'b1;
            end else begin
                scan_timer <= scan_timer + 1'b1;
                scan_tick  <= 1'b0;
            end
        end
    end

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 2. Double-Flop Synchronizer for Async Row Inputs
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            row_sync1 <= 4'b1111; // Default to unpressed (pull-ups high)
            row_sync2 <= 4'b1111;
        end else begin
            row_sync1 <= row_pins;
            row_sync2 <= row_sync1;
        end
    end

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 3. Matrix Column Cycling & Key Capture Logic
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Row detection logic: any active-low row bit zero indicates a key press
    logic key_detected_current_col;
    assign key_detected_current_col = (row_sync2 != 4'b1111);

    always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            col_select    <= 2 me0;
            col_pins_reg  <= 4'b1110; // Col 0 active low
            key_valid_reg <= 1'b0;
            key_code_reg  <= 4'h0;
        end else begin
            // Sample rows and update scan position on each tick
            if (scan_tick) begin
                if (key_detected_current_col) begin
                    // Key detected on active column: hold column active and output key code
                    key_valid_reg <= 1'b1;
                    
                    case ({col_select, row_sync2})
                        // Col 0 (Active-Low Column 0: 4'b1110)
                        6'b00_1110: key_code_reg <= 4'h1; // Row 0 -> '1'
                        6'b00_1101: key_code_reg <= 4'h4; // Row 1 -> '4'
                        6'b00_1011: key_code_reg <= 4'h7; // Row 2 -> '7'
                        6'b00_0111: key_code_reg <= 4'h0; // Row 3 -> '0'

                        // Col 1 (Active-Low Column 1: 4'b1101)
                        6'b01_1110: key_code_reg <= 4'h2; // Row 0 -> '2'
                        6'b01_1101: key_code_reg <= 4'h5; // Row 1 -> '5'
                        6'b01_1011: key_code_reg <= 4'h8; // Row 2 -> '8'
                        6'b01_0111: key_code_reg <= 4'hF; // Row 3 -> 'F' / 'A'

                        // Col 2 (Active-Low Column 2: 4'b1011)
                        6'b10_1110: key_code_reg <= 4'h3; // Row 0 -> '3'
                        6'b10_1101: key_code_reg <= 4'h6; // Row 1 -> '6'
                        6'b10_1011: key_code_reg <= 4'h9; // Row 2 -> '9'
                        6'b10_0111: key_code_reg <= 4'hE; // Row 3 -> 'E' / 'B'

                        // Col 3 (Active-Low Column 3: 4'b0111)
                        6'b11_1110: key_code_reg <= 4'hA; // Row 0 -> 'A' / 'C'
                        6'b11_1101: key_code_reg <= 4'hB; // Row 1 -> 'B' / 'D'
                        6'b11_1011: key_code_reg <= 4'hC; // Row 2 -> 'C' / '*'
                        6'b11_0111: key_code_reg <= 4'hD; // Row 3 -> 'D' / '#'

                        default:    key_code_reg <= key_code_reg;
                    endcase

                end else if (key_valid_reg) begin
                    // Key was previously pressed on this column but has now been released
                    key_valid_reg <= 1'b0;

                end else begin
                    // No key active: advance to next active-low column
                    col_select   <= col_select + 1'b1;
                    col_pins_reg <= ~(4'b0001 << (col_select + 1'b1));
                end
            end
        end
    end

    // Drive output ports from registers
    assign col_pins      = col_pins_reg;
    assign raw_key_valid = key_valid_reg;
    assign raw_key_code  = key_code_reg;

endmodule
```

### Key Design Elements
- **Standard Keypad Mapping:** Decodes standard 4x4 matrix layouts (0–9, A–F) based on active-low
  row/column grid intersections.
- **Scan Pause on Detection:** When a row activation is detected, scanning pauses on that active
  column.
  `raw_key_valid` stays high and `raw_key_code` holds stable as long as the key is pressed. 
- **iCE40 Pin
  Setup:** Rows require internal pull-up resistors, which can be specified in your Physical
  Constraints File (`.pcf`) as `set_io -pullup yes row_pins[*]`. 
- **Metastability Safety:** Mechanical contact bounces entering `row_pins` pass through a 2-stage
  synchronizer (`row_sync1`, `row_sync2`) before evaluation.

Here is the complete top-level SystemVerilog module targeting the Lattice iCE40 UP5K FPGA. It uses
the iCE40 primitive `SB_HFOSC` to generate an internal clock, integrates the keypad scanner and
one-shot modules, maintains a 2-digit shift register, and time-multiplexes a dual 7-segment display
for flicker-free operation.

```systemverilog
module keypad_top (
    // Matrix physical pins (active-low)
    input  logic [3:0] row_pins,
    output logic [3:0] col_pins,

    // Dual 7-segment physical pins (active-low)
    output logic [6:0] seg_pins,  // Segments A-G
    output logic [1:0] digit_sel  // Digit select drivers (active-low)
);

    // =========================================================================
    // 1. Clock Generation via iCE40 High-Frequency Internal Oscillator
    // =========================================================================
    logic clk;

    // SB_HFOSC Primitive Configured for 12 MHz Output (CLKHF_DIV = "0b10")
    SB_HFOSC #(
        .CLKHF_DIV("0b10")
    ) u_hfosc (
        .CLKHFPU(1'b1), // Power up oscillator
        .CLKHFEN(1 me1), // Enable oscillator output
        .CLKHF(clk)     // ~12 MHz output clock
    );

    // Synchronous Reset Generator
    logic [3:0] rst_cnt = 4'h0;
    logic       rst_n;

    always_ff @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst_cnt != 4'hF) begin
            rst_cnt <= rst_cnt + 1'b1;
            rst_n   <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            rst_n   <= 1'b1;
        end
    end

    // =========================================================================
    // 2. Keypad Subsystem Instantiations
    // =========================================================================
    logic       raw_key_valid;
    logic [3:0] raw_key_code;
    logic       new_key_strobe;
    logic [3:0] key_code;

    // Continuous Matrix Scanner
    keypad_scanner #(
        .CLK_FREQ_HZ(12_000_000),
        .SCAN_FREQ_HZ(1000)
    ) u_scanner (
        .clk          (clk),
        .rst_n        (rst_n),
        .row_pins     (row_pins),
        .col_pins     (col_pins),
        .raw_key_valid(raw_key_valid),
        .raw_key_code (raw_key_code)
    );

    // Debouncer & One-Shot Registration
    keypad_oneshot #(
        .CLK_FREQ_HZ(12_000_000),
        .DEBOUNCE_MS(10)
    ) u_oneshot (
        .clk           (clk),
        .rst_n         (rst_n),
        .raw_key_valid (raw_key_valid),
        .raw_key_code  (raw_key_code),
        .new_key_strobe(new_key_strobe),
        .key_code      (key_code)
    );

    // =========================================================================
    // 3. 2-Digit History Shift Register
    // =========================================================================
    logic [3:0] digit_recent;
    logic [3:0] digit_older;

    always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            digit_recent <= 4'h0;
            digit_older  <= 4'h0;
        end else if (new_key_strobe) begin
            digit_older  <= digit_recent; // Shift old digit
            digit_recent <= key_code;    // Insert newest digit
        end
    end

    // =========================================================================
    // 4. Time-Multiplexed Display Driver (~200 Hz Refresh Rate)
    // =========================================================================
    // 12 MHz / 200 Hz / 2 digits = 30,000 cycles per digit state (~600 Hz toggle)
    localparam int MUX_DIV_CYCLES = 30_000;
    localparam int MUX_DIV_WIDTH  = $clog2(MUX_DIV_CYCLES);

    logic [MUX_DIV_WIDTH-1:0] mux_timer;
    logic                     mux_sel; // 0 = Digit 0 (older), 1 = Digit 1 (recent)

    always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            mux_timer <= '0;
            mux_sel   <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            if (mux_timer >= MUX_DIV_CYCLES - 1) begin
                mux_timer <= '0;
                mux_sel   <= ~mux_sel; // Swap active digit
            end else begin
                mux_timer <= mux_timer + 1'b1;
            end
        end
    end

    // Digit Selection & Active Hex Data Muxing
    logic [3:0] current_hex;

    always_comb begin
        if (mux_sel) begin
            digit_sel   = 2'b10;        // Select Digit 1 (active-low driver)
            current_hex = digit_recent;
        end else begin
            digit_sel   = 2'b01;        // Select Digit 0 (active-low driver)
            current_hex = digit_older;
        end
    end

    // 7-Segment Decoder Conversion (Common Anode / Active-Low Segments)
    sevenSegment u_decoder (
        .hex_digit(current_hex),
        .seg_out  (seg_pins)
    );

endmodule
```

### Module Architecture & Features
1. Integrated `SB_HFOSC` Oscillator: Instantiates the built-in iCE40 oscillator primitive configured
   for 12 MHz. An internal power-on reset generator (`rst_cnt`) safely releases the system from
   reset after power-up.
2. Key Code Shift Logic: When `new_key_strobe` fires for a single cycle, `digit_older` receives the
   value of `digit_recent`, and `digit_recent` absorbs the new `key_code`. The display registers
   remain untouched until a validated key press occurs.
3. Flicker-Free Display Driver: Uses a 30,000-cycle timer to toggle digit enablement at 600 Hz (300
   Hz per digit frame). This eliminates visible flicker and maintains uniform brightness across both
   digits.
4. Physical Pin Constraints (`.pcf`): Pin drivers assume active-low signals for the matrix keypad rows
   (requiring internal pull-ups enabled in `.pcf`) and active-low digit/segment drives typical of
   common-anode 7-segment displays.
